name: Exact Common-Section-First Substitution Width
statement: Let $H=C_0\cap C_1$ be nonempty and meet every coordinate interval $[x,z]$ with $x\in C_0$ and $z\in C_1$. For $F_0=T$, $F_1=T^{\mathrm c}$, $D=C\circ_iT$, and $I=H\times\{0,1\}^Y$, one has $\sigma(D;I)=\max(\{\sigma(C_0;H),\sigma(C_1;H)\}\cup\{\sigma(F_b):C_b\setminus H\ne\emptyset\})$.
proof: Order the whole common fiber first, then the exclusive fibers on each side using optimal $H$-first outer orders and optimal inner orders. Same-fiber predecessors use inner witnesses and same-side predecessors use outer witnesses in completed fibers. For an opposite-side predecessor, the interval hypothesis supplies a point of $H$ between the two outside words, and the outer order gives a contained witness toward it without any inner-coordinate cost. Conditioning an inner word recovers each pair $(C_b,H)$, while conditioning an exclusive outside word recovers the relevant test side, giving all reverse bounds.
